jobs.description:
**Build with us

**Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow – with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.

With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.

We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.

Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.

**Your impact

**This is your chance to build Mollie's presence in Denmark from the ground up, as the first person hired with this market as your sole focus. You won't be starting from zero: you'll have the Nordic foundation already built in Sweden to work from, but the Danish playbook is yours to write.

You'll open the market, land our first Danish customers, and turn early learnings into a repeatable approach we can scale. It's a broader, more entrepreneurial scope than a standard sales role. You'll work deals from $100K a month while building toward bigger opportunities of up to $1 million a month, all while shaping how Mollie understands and enters this market for the long run.

What makes this role stand out is the mix: outbound selling, customer discovery, partnerships, and competitive analysis, all rolled into one seat with real ownership. If you want to build something rather than maintain something, this is that opportunity.

**What You'll Ship

**

• Run outbound sales and manage the full sales process, including around 20 cold calls a week

• Build a Danish pipeline and land Mollie's first customers in the market

• Gather market feedback and grow larger opportunities, including deals of up to $1 million a month

• Build relationships with Danish agencies and work on partnerships alongside the partner manager based in Stockholm

• Share what you learn about the Danish marketing landscape with the marketing team to help shape events and go-to-market plans

• Run competitive analysis to sharpen how Mollie positions itself in Denmark

**What You'll Bring

**

• Around 5 years of full-cycle sales experience, with a strong outbound track record and demonstrated success in structured cold outreach

• Value selling capability, with a data-driven approach to activity and pipeline management

• Strong negotiation and contract handling skills, including experience communicating and negotiating with C-level stakeholders

• Creativity in building a pipeline through partnerships or marketing outreach (you don't need to have done this before, just show the potential)

• Experience in payments, fintech, or SaaS sales, built across multiple companies

• Comfortable working hands-on in a role with broad scope and real uncertainty

• Fluency in Danish

**Grow your way

**At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy

If you're excited by the idea of building what's next, for yourself and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV (in English) using the form below.

Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie is really like.

**AI at Mollie

**We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every team, every role, every day.

AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance with us.

Your impact begins here

As GLP QA Professional, you will help make sure non-clinical research at Novo is carried out to Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) standards. You will oversee studies, inspect internal and external work, and turn what you see into clear, practical recommendations that keep research reliable and moving. You will shape how quality is built into non-clinical processes, strengthening the foundation for treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You bring a balanced, practical quality mindset. You work systematically and independently, take initiative and stay flexible when priorities change. To succeed in this role, you have:

• Experience as a laboratory technician and relevant qualification, or a master’s degree in science, pharmacy, medicine or a similar field.

• Experience within GLP, for example from quality assurance, GLP-regulated work, non-clinical research or laboratory activities.

• Knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS) and the ability to interpret and communicate regulatory and procedural requirements.

• Strong analytical and organisational skills, with attention to detail and the ability to work systematically and independently.

• Strong collaboration and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to build constructive relationships with internal colleagues and external Contract Research Organisations (CROs).

• Proficiency in written and spoken English, and confidence in communicating observations, recommendations and quality matters.

Desirable, but not essential:

Experience from industrial drug development.

What you’ll do

You will be the quality partner for GLP-regulated activities, helping colleagues and CROs meet requirements while keeping study quality and compliance protected.

• Perform quality oversight and compliance verification of GLP-regulated activities, including review of study plans, reports, relevant SOPs and documentation from internal areas and external CROs.

• Plan and conduct study-based and process-based internal inspections, including Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP) activities where relevant.

• Support stakeholders on GLP requirements and general quality matters, including review of GLP action plans from internal and external audits.

• Contribute to maintaining and improving the department’s QMS, including harmonisation, digitalisation and simplification initiatives.

• Communicate observations, regulatory requirements and practical quality recommendations clearly to internal and external stakeholders, and take part in relevant projects, audits and regulatory inspections.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Non-Clinical Quality, a diverse team of 15 skilled colleagues in Søborg. It is one of two sister departments within Process Management, Non-Clinical, IT & AI Quality, part of R&D Quality. In R&D, curiosity, data, collaboration and operational excellence come together to advance scientific ideas towards clinical testing, and Non-Clinical Quality helps make sure the processes behind that work are fit for purpose.

The team provides QMS expertise to a global organisation and works closely with stakeholders across the value chain. You will have many interfaces: research and laboratory colleagues in internal areas, external CROs and other collaboration partners, and teams across the organisation working on improvement projects.

You will work in an international environment where clear communication helps you build trust, create clarity around requirements and keep work moving. Some travel may be required for audits and other GLP QA activities.

What you can expect here

You will build your GLP expertise and take on increasing responsibility, with room to influence how quality is embedded in non-clinical research processes. Alongside day-to-day oversight, you will contribute to cross-organisational improvement projects and share ideas that improve methods, systems and processes.

You will be supported to perform at your best, trusted to work independently and encouraged to make your voice heard. You will grow through practical experience, close collaboration with colleagues and continuous learning.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200.00 to

838,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate's skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here

Start now

Your impact begins today, so apply by 13 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We are an equal opportunities employer and are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all applicants.

jobs.occupation: Senior Data Engineer - Supply Chain AI Solutions
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Senior Data Engineer, you will build the data foundations that bring Supply Chain AI Solutions to life. You will turn complex requirements into scalable, compliant, production-ready data products and pipelines that power strategic AI use cases for the Supply Chain organisation. Working hands-on in Databricks, you will help move ideas into reliable operation, supporting resilient supply chains and the delivery of treatment to millions of people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You bring strong production delivery experience and the ability to lead the data engineering side of an AI use case, from idea to reliable operation.

• 
A Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science or a related field.

• 
At least 8 years of experience in data engineering, including 3+ years in a senior role.

• 
Deep expertise in Azure Databricks, including Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Workflows and Databricks SQL.

• 
Strong proficiency in Python, Apache Spark and SQL, with proven experience designing and building scalable, production-ready data pipelines and data products.

• 
A solid understanding of BI concepts, dimensional modelling, report and semantic layers, data integrations and self-service data platforms.

• 
Hands-on experience with DevOps practices, CI/CD pipelines, GitHub, coding best practices and agile ways of working such as Scrum.

• 
Professional proficiency in English, with the ability to communicate clearly with technical teams, business stakeholders and colleagues at different levels of the organisation.

You are technically curious and enjoy building data products that make a real difference. You are structured, take ownership, drive direction and inspire others to keep improving, and you stay on top of the latest trends in data engineering and AI.

Useful, but not essential:

• 
A Databricks Certified Data Engineer (Professional) certification or another relevant data engineering or cloud certification.

• 
Familiarity with Azure and AWS cloud services.

• 
Experience with Power BI or similar BI tools.

What you’ll do

You will set the critical path for Data Engineering within the delivery team to ensure we deliver reliable, production-ready products for our use cases, while sharing your expertise and support team members in adopting best practices. This includes being a hands-on technical contributor who is comfortable in taking the lead in building the required data products for use case from the early phase all the way to production.

• 
Design and implement data and model pipelines in Databricks, using Unity Catalog for governance and medallion architecture patterns to organise and serve reliable data.

• 
Apply an AI-first engineering mindset to create robust, scalable data foundations that are ready for future AI-driven manufacturing and supply chain use cases.

• 
Work hands-on across the full engineering lifecycle, from data modelling and pipeline development to testing, deployment, monitoring and continuous improvement.

• 
Build high-quality data products and pipelines within our established Databricks platform and engineering framework, with a focus on performance, cost efficiency, governance, compliance and maintainability

• 
Turn complex requirements into clear engineering priorities, identifying the critical path and making pragmatic decisions about what to solve now, what to simplify and what to develop further over time

• 
Mentor and develop data engineers through design sparring, code reviews and practical coaching.

This is a hands-on engineering role where you will spend the majority of your time designing, building and improving solutions, while also providing technical guidance to less experienced engineers. You will work closely with the Lead Data Engineer and other senior technical colleagues, contributing to engineering direction while focusing on turning that direction into high-quality, working solutions.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Enterprise AI within Enterprise IT & Quality, where colleagues work across the Novo value chain, stay close to stakeholders and help deliver trusted technology and high quality. Your team is Supply Chain AI Solutions: a small, end-to-end team where data scientists and engineers work side by side, combining analytical depth with the engineering capability to bring solutions into production.

Your closest colleagues are the Tech Lead, the Lead Data Scientist and the AI Product Owner. You will also collaborate with engineers, architects, data scientists and business stakeholders in the Supply Chain organisation, acting as a senior technical contributor across teams. Together, you will make clear decisions, keep delivery moving and turn practical needs into better operational decisions.

The team is cloud-native, working with platforms such as Databricks, Azure and AWS. It values agility, diverse thinking and continuous learning, and its culture is built on feedback, honesty and fun. The role is based in Ballerup, Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership, share your voice and shape how data engineering is built within Supply Chain AI Solutions. You will keep growing through continuous learning and career development, working on AI use cases at the forefront of technology, alongside colleagues who raise the bar with you.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 to 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy heree.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn complex data needs into reliable AI-ready products for Supply Chain, apply for the Senior Data Engineer role by November 10th 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For questions, please reach out to Mikkel Bjerregaard Ditlevsen, MBDV@novonordisk.com.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Role - Advanced IT System Management Professional

Location - Hilleroed

Contract: Temporary position – 1-year fixed-term contract.

Your impact begins here

As Advanced IT System Management Professional, you will keep the IT Systems and Computerized Equipment behind Materials & Device Analytics QC reliable, compliant and fit for purpose. Over one year, you will drive continuous improvement, keep compliance documentation current and give laboratory users a clear point of contact. Your work helps ensure our global production sites have the materials they need to operate efficiently and meet patient demand.

What you’ll bring

• A bachelor’s degree in Science, Engineering, Computer Science or a related discipline.

• A minimum of 3 years’ experience in IT System or Computerized Equipment management.

• A structured, detail-oriented approach and a clear focus on quality.

• A proactive, solution-oriented mindset, strong communication skills and a collaborative way of supporting colleagues.

• Professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

Useful, but not essential:

Experience from the pharmaceutical industry or another regulated industry.

What you’ll do

You will hold a key role in IT governance and compliance for a portfolio of IT Systems and Computerized Equipment within Materials & Device Analytics QC, driving continuous improvement as you go.

• Support life cycle management and contribute to smaller projects, so IT Systems and Computerized Equipment remain compliant with all applicable requirements.

• Maintain compliance documentation and standard operating procedures (SOPs), keeping them accurate, up to date and easy to access.

• Act as a technical resource in implementation projects and share your knowledge across the team.

• Align and manage stakeholder and user expectations for IT Systems and Computerized Equipment.

• Serve as the primary point of contact for local users, Project Managers, Validation Managers, System Owners and Quality Assurance (QA).

Who you’ll work with

You will join Sourcing LABS IT, part of Computerised Laboratory Systems in the Laboratory, Planning & Eco-systems area. We are the IT and systems partner for the Materials & Device Analytics QC laboratories and GMP Materials Analytical Science & Technology. Together, these areas cover raw materials, devices, primary and printed packaging, specifications and quality control prior to production release.

You will be part of a team of nine colleagues in Denmark, supported by three Compliance Supporters in Brazil, so close cross-border collaboration is part of everyday work. Your closest partners will be local users, Project Managers, Validation Managers, System Owners and QA. The position is based in Hillerød, Denmark. You will have broad ownership and the opportunity to influence how laboratory technologies are implemented and used across multiple sites.

What you can expect here

You will join a collaborative team that values expertise and invests in professional development. You will be trusted to take ownership, make your voice heard and grow your skills through hands-on project work and knowledge sharing with colleagues in Denmark and Brazil.

This is a 1-year fixed-term position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Your impact begins here

Clinical data has the greatest value when it is reliable, accessible and ready to support the decisions that matter. As a Senior Clinical Data Management Professional you will lead end-to-end data management for global clinical trials, helping ensure high-quality data from protocol development through submission.

You will combine hands-on trial leadership with strategic thinking, bringing functions and partners together to manage complexity, strengthen data quality and develop better ways of working.

What you'll bring

You are a proactive and collaborative clinical data management professional who can turn complex requirements into clear priorities and high-quality delivery.

To succeed in this role, you will bring:

• A BSc or MSc in IT, Natural Sciences, Life Sciences or an equivalent field

• At least 3 years of experience within clinical data management or an equivalent area

• Experience leading trials or projects in an international environment with increasing complexity

• Strong project management and stakeholder management skills

• A good understanding of data management processes, clinical data flow, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and regulatory requirements

• Fluency in written and spoken English

You bring analytical rigour, accountability and sound judgement to your work. You are also comfortable challenging established ways of working and contributing to innovative solutions or new methodologies.

What you'll do

You will take ownership of clinical data management activities across the trial lifecycle. Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead data management planning, timelines and priorities, aligning deliverables with overall trial goals

• Develop and maintain data management plans and other key trial documentation

• Shape effective trial design by providing data management input to protocols and defining data collection requirements and risks

• Drive data quality and integrity while coordinating risks and issues with relevant stakeholders

• Support submission deliverables, data access processes, regulatory compliance, and trial-level audit and inspection readiness

• Partner with the Project Clinical Data Manager on project-level alignment, inspection readiness and vendor assessments within your area of expertise

Who you'll work with

You will join Clinical Data Management within Clinical Data Management & Programming, a global organisation responsible for the planning, execution, quality and delivery of clinical trial data across Novo Nordisk's development portfolio.

Your work will connect you with Project Clinical Data Managers, project leadership, cross-functional colleagues and external partners. Together, you will manage data from protocol development through database lock and regulatory submission, while contributing to cross-trial alignment and effective data strategies.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to work with global clinical trial portfolios where your expertise can directly shape how complex clinical data is planned, collected and delivered. You will be able to contribute ideas, challenge existing approaches and help develop better ways of working while collaborating across functions and geographies.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000.00 to 956,900.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience. We are looking for different experience levels, therefore we will determine the relevant level and salary based on a collective assessment.

As Global Advanced Analytics Lead, you will apply statistical modelling and machine learning to commercial questions that matter for Novo’s portfolio and launches. You will turn commercial and real-world data into insights that help teams understand market and patient dynamics and assess commercial opportunities. The role combines hands-on analytical work with direct business engagement. You will take ownership of analytical projects, from shaping the question and building the model to explaining what the findings mean for the decision ahead.

As Novo strengthens its core business and builds future growth opportunities, understanding changing patient needs, consumer behaviour and market dynamics is increasingly important. Your work will support Product & Portfolio Strategy in sharpening global strategies, strengthening portfolio competitiveness and preparing for successful launches.

What you’ll bring

You bring hands-on analytical skill and the judgement to turn it into decisions people can act on.

• A master’s degree in data science, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Life Sciences, Business Administration or a related field, with strong quantitative and applied analytics expertise.

• 5+ years in advanced analytics, applied data science or statistical modelling, including hands-on delivery of analytical projects.

• Strong practical capability in Python or R, and in SQL for data extraction and preparation.

• Experience building and validating statistical and machine learning models, and assessing their performance, uncertainty and limitations.

• Experience with complex datasets, reproducible code, version control and technical documentation.

• The ability to translate findings into business recommendations and explain them clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

• Structured problem-solving, openness about uncertainty and limitations, and sound judgement on when to seek guidance or escalate.

Useful, but not essential:

• A PhD or a strong research background.

• Pharmaceutical commercial analytics or healthcare real-world data experience, particularly segmentation and launch uptake modelling.

What you’ll do

You will own the hands-on delivery of advanced analytics projects that inform portfolio and commercial decisions. Your responsibilities will include:

• Translate business questions into analytical approaches, working with stakeholders to clarify the decision, scope and intended outcomes.

• Develop and refine predictive models, patient segmentation models and launch uptake analyses to understand commercial opportunities and changing market dynamics.

• Investigate complex commercial and real-world datasets, applying statistical and machine learning methods suited to the question.

• Translate findings into clear recommendations, explaining their commercial implications and discussing them directly with stakeholders.

• Build reliable, reproducible analyses, validating model performance and making assumptions, uncertainty and data limitations clear.

• Collaborate with BI, Data Governance and enterprise technical partners to ensure analytical outputs can be maintained and used effectively.

• Propose new analytical questions, share reusable code and contribute practical improvements to the team’s methods.

The role is base in Søborg, Denmark.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Data, Analytics & AI Strategy team within Product & Portfolio Strategy (PPS). PPS brings together commercial strategy, medical affairs and business development across therapy areas to guide Novo’s portfolio and strengthen its competitiveness.

Your projects will connect you with colleagues across Portfolio Strategy, Insights & Access, Commercial Units, Global Medical Affairs and Business Development, depending on the business question. You will also collaborate with R&D, US and International Operations, Enterprise IT and technical partners.

You will work closely with the Advanced Analytics Associate Director on analytical design, methodological choices and interpretation of findings. You will own hands-on delivery of your projects, with the Associate Director providing technical direction, challenge and review. This partnership combines independent analytical ownership with close technical collaboration.

What you can expect here

You will work on technically challenging questions with clear commercial relevance, combining hands-on modelling with direct collaboration across the global business. The role offers ownership of analytical delivery, close partnership with experienced colleagues and the opportunity to see your findings inform portfolio and launch decisions. You will also contribute ideas and reusable approaches that strengthen how the team applies advanced analytics. At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Medical Writing Specialist

Regulatory Scientific Writing

Søborg, Denmark

Are you an experienced Medical Writer ready to shape scientific communication across global clinical development? Join us as a Medical Writing Specialist and play a key role in producing high-quality clinical documentation, influencing strategic decisions and driving improved ways of working across therapeutic areas.

Your new role

In this specialist position you will contribute both deep scientific expertise and strategic thinking to our Regulatory Scientific Writing organisation. You will be responsible for delivering high-quality clinical documents while also acting as a key driver for alignment, collaboration and process improvements across development projects.

You will:

· deliver a broad range of regulatory medical writing tasks to a consistently high stand-ard.

· act as Project Lead or Track Lead on assigned projects, ensuring alignment across stake-holders.

· represent Regulatory Scientific Writing in cross-functional discussions and project groups.

· share better practices, mentor colleagues and contribute to capability building.

· lead process optimisation initiatives and help develop innovative solutions that support our strategic ambitions.

This role is office-based in Søborg, Denmark, and you will collaborate closely with global col-leagues across functions and therapeutic areas.

Your new department

You will join Regulatory Scientific Writing, the medical writing function at Novo, consisting of ap-proximately 200 medical writers across the globe. We are part of Development which oversees clinical drug development and submissions to authorities worldwide - from early-stage research to market authorisation.

Our department combines strong scientific expertise with a collaborative mindset. We focus on transforming complex clinical data into clear, concise and impactful communication. We value continuous learning, a supportive culture and a drive for simplicity in our ways of working.

Your skills and qualifications

To succeed in this role, you have:

· a Master’s degree within natural sciences (e.g. M.Sc., M.Sc. Pharm. or equivalent), ideally supplemented with a PhD, and at least 5 years of relevant medical writing experience in the pharmaceutical industry.

· an expert understanding of clinical development, regulatory requirements and clinical documentation.

· full proficiency in written and spoken English.

On a personal level you work independently with complex tasks and bring a strong analytical mindset. You handle fluctuating workloads, navigate uncertainty confidently and communicate clearly by transforming complex data into understandable content. You naturally build relation-ships, collaborate across cultures and act as an informal leader and mentor. You think strategi-cally and are comfortable influencing both project and organisational goals.

Working at Novo Nordisk

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways for-ward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. When you join us, you're not just starting a job – you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

What we offer

There is, of course, more on offer here than the uniqueness of our culture and the extraordi-nary results we produce. Being part of a global healthcare company means opportunities to learn and develop are all around us, while our benefits are designed with your career and life stage in mind.

Department: R&D Tech Delivery****Location: Søborg, Denmark

Your impact begins here

Join R&D Tech Delivery as an Interim Department Assistant, where you will help the VP and Leadership Team stay focused on the priorities that matter most. You will bring structure to a fast-moving environment, keep key leadership activities on track and take ownership of selected improvement initiatives. By turning complex input into clear actions, communications and decision-ready materials, you will help the team operate effectively and keep priorities moving forward.

This is an interim role from February to End August 2027.

What you’ll bring

You combine strong executive support skills with the confidence to take ownership, create structure and work effectively with senior stakeholders. You are comfortable moving between hands-on administrative tasks and broader operational activities.

To succeed in this role, you have:

• Experience as a Personal Assistant, Executive Assistant or in a comparable senior business-support role, with experience supporting senior stakeholders at VP level.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to create clear, high-quality presentations and executive-level materials.

• Strong execution and organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple activities, follow through and bring structure to a fast-moving workload.

• Confidence to speak up, exercise discretion and handle confidential and sensitive information appropriately.

• Strong working knowledge of PowerPoint and experience using ChatGPT and Copilot in your work.

• Experience with Claude or similar tools as an advantage.

• Professional fluency in spoken and written English.

What you’ll do

• Provide proactive executive support to the VP, managing priorities, meetings and a complex calendar while anticipating what is needed to keep work moving.

• Coordinate Leadership Team meetings and activities, including agendas, materials, decisions, actions and structured follow-up.

• Take ownership of selected operational projects and process-improvement initiatives, turning broad direction into clear actions and driving them through to completion.

• Create clear executive communications, presentations and decision materials, turning complex or incomplete input into concise, audience-focused messages.

• Work confidently across stakeholders, following up on priorities, identifying emerging issues and helping maintain momentum across concurrent activities.

• Support the practical running of the organisation through activities such as workforce coordination, onboarding and offboarding, procurement and maintaining relevant information structures.

Who you’ll work with

You will work closely with the VP of R&D Tech Delivery and the R&D Tech Delivery Leadership Team, becoming a trusted point of coordination across leadership activities and priorities. You will collaborate with Personal and Executive Assistants across the wider organisation as well as colleagues in HR, Finance, Procurement, IT and Facilities, alongside internal and external partners. The role sits within a large stakeholder environment, with the department comprising approximately 190 employees and 500 external consultants.

What you can expect here

You can expect a role where your contribution is visible and where you have the opportunity to bring structure, take ownership and help important work move forward. Working closely with senior stakeholders, you will have room to use your judgement, contribute ideas and make an impact beyond day-to-day executive support.

You’ll join an environment where collaboration, curiosity and different perspectives are valued, with opportunities to contribute and develop while helping the organisation deliver on its priorities.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Are you eager to influence the future direction of Arla Foods? Do you envision yourself as a future leader?

How will you make an impact?

The Arla F15 Graduate Programme is a two-year, international development programme designed for graduates who want to learn quickly, explore different areas of a global business and grow into future leadership opportunities.`

Through three eight-month rotations, you will work on meaningful business projects, build an international network and develop the confidence, skills and experience to make an impact at Arla. Business areas for projects may include Marketing, Sales, HR, Strategy, Sustainability, Business Development, and Supply Chain. We will match you with a suitable department based on business needs and your profile, offering you the chance to learn and make a difference. Your F15 Graduate journey begins on 1st September 2027.

• First rotation (8 months - Aarhus, Denmark) Based at one of our offices in Aarhus you will be assigned a strategically important project somewhere in the business.

• Second rotation (8 months - Outside Denmark) You will have more influence over your second project assignment, which will give you the opportunity to continue growing in a meaningful way whilst adding real value to Arla.

• Third rotation (8 months - Any Arla market) You will collaborate with the business to source potential high impact projects for your third rotation. You will have the most influence over projects during your final rotation.

What will make you a successful F15 Graduate?

To apply for the F15 Graduate Programme, please ensure that you meet the following criteria

• You should either be in the process of completing, or have completed, a bachelor’s or master’s degree between September 2025 and September 2027. We welcome diverse educational backgrounds but seek candidates with a strong drive towards a business-focused career.

• International experience gained from working, studying or volunteering abroad is an advantage.

• Preferably at least one year of relevant work experience from student jobs or a minimum of six months of internship experience.

• You are globally mobile and willing to go on one or two rotations abroad during the two-year programme. As your first rotation is based in Aarhus, Denmark you will need to relocate unless you already reside in the local area. Arla Foods will support you with this relocation.

This programme will suit graduates who have leadership aspirations and an ambitious mindset, which combines strategic thinking with a passion for results. A global mindset is essential, as is the ability to build positive relationships and strong influencing skills. The ideal candidate should be curious, competitive, and open to change, demonstrating resilience, while also being humble, self-aware, and open to feedback.

Throughout the rotations you will receive a variety of development opportunities every step of the way. To ensure your professional and personal development, you will benefit from

• Responsibilities from day one, enabling on-the-job learning in three different areas

• Graduate development camps, taking place in different markets with your graduate colleagues

• One-to-one mentoring and sparring from senior leaders

• Be part of a supportive graduate community across all Arla Futures programmes

Important information before applying

The application period for the F15 Graduate Programme runs from 2nd November 2026 until 23.59 CET on 3rd January 2027. Before applying, please ensure you have prepared your CV and cover letter in English. You will be asked a series of questions on the application page, so we recommend that you start the application process from a computer instead of a mobile phone.

For additional information, read more about the F15 Graduate Programme on our website. Here, you can get inspiration from some of our previous and current F15s and learn more about the programme. You can also read more about what to expect from the recruitment process.

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

Job Title: AI Solution Lead

Department: Enterprise IT and Quality

Location: Ballerup, Denmark

Your impact begins here

As AI Solution Lead in Quality AI, you will turn opportunities for AI into working applications and agents for complex, regulated pharmaceutical quality processes. You will own initiatives from problem definition through to adoption, combining hands-on development with technical and stakeholder leadership. You will also help shape how AI can be shown to be fit for its intended use. Your work helps quality teams act faster, with evidence they can trust.

What you’ll bring

• A Master’s degree or PhD in a relevant field.

• Experience leading AI/ML initiatives or working on AI products, with direct responsibility for delivering working solutions – for example as a founder, engineer, researcher or technical consultant.

• Practical experience building with LLMs, assessing architecture, investigating technical problems and working directly with code.

• Experience structuring business problems, connecting business needs to technical choices and explaining trade-offs to different audiences.

• The ability to build confidence with business leaders, challenge assumptions, negotiate priorities and turn discussions into decisions.

• Ownership and initiative when responsibilities or requirements are unclear, and comfort making decisions with incomplete information.

• Clear communication and the curiosity to learn pharmaceutical quality requirements – and the judgement to question how they are implemented.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience working in regulated environments.

What you’ll do

You will lead assigned AI initiatives in Quality AI, from the first conversation with process owners to the point where users rely on what you have built.

• Work with process owners and users to identify opportunities, define what success looks like and prioritise what to build.

• Lead delivery across engineers, quality experts, business stakeholders and IT – resolving dependencies and securing the decisions needed to keep moving.

• Shape solution architecture and guide choices about models, data, integrations and evaluation.

• Prototype, code and troubleshoot when your direct involvement helps delivery.

• Establish evaluations and acceptance criteria, and use the evidence to guide development and deployment decisions.

• Take initiatives through implementation and adoption, tracking delivery against the agreed business outcomes, and build reusable components, tools and practices that help later initiatives move faster.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Quality AI team in Enterprise IT & Quality, where colleagues work across the Novo value chain, stay close to stakeholders and help deliver trusted technology and high quality. You will work with a high degree of independence and may guide the work of less experienced colleagues, keeping delivery on track against timelines, quality standards and strategic objectives.

Your closest partners will be pharmaceutical quality process owners and users, engineers, quality experts, IT teams, and business leaders and senior stakeholders. Together you will agree priorities, settle trade-offs and make decisions across functions, so good ideas move from discussion to working applications without losing pace. The role is based in Ballerup, Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will have room to lead. You will be trusted to make decisions on AI/ML approaches, data products and architecture, and to challenge established ways of working when a simpler, faster route meets quality and compliance requirements. Clear expectations and honest, open dialogue with colleagues help you deliver your best work.

You will also grow your expertise: building AI for a regulated environment, learning pharmaceutical quality requirements from the experts who work with them every day, and helping define approaches that other initiatives will build on.

Salary

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 to 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn AI into trusted, working tools for pharmaceutical quality, apply for the AI Solution Lead role by 15 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Do you love designing clean game architecture, building multiplayer systems that run smoothly, and helping a team of programmers make the right technical decisions? Great! Let’s talk.

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

We're building something unannounced, exciting, thoroughly goofy, and built to be played together online. We're now looking for a Lead Game Programmer to help building the underlying systems that make it all work, from the core architecture to the multiplayer tech that connects our players. You'll stay hands-on in the code and the Unity editor while helping the programming team make good technical decisions, stay aligned, and build systems that support creative experimentation. And just to be very clear: this is a technical leadership role, not a people-management position.

**Here’s What That Looks Like Day To Day

**

• In collaboration with game designers, artists, and other programmers, you’ll build new features and systems and continuously iterate on improvements. We all work in Unity with C#, with every team member hands-on in the editor

• You’ll set and communicate the project’s technical direction, turning creative goals and production needs into clear technical priorities

• You’ll help the programming team make architectural decisions, align around shared patterns, and navigate trade-offs between long-term code health and short-term needs

• You’ll review and improve technical solutions, share best practices, and support other programmers without becoming a gatekeeper or bottleneck

• You’ll proactively identify technical risks, messy systems, and missing foundations, and take responsibility for addressing them at the right time

• Overall, you’ll make sure the project is technically healthy and maintain the codebase in a way that makes it easy for others to build on

**This includes things like...

**

• Designing an architecture that allows for easy gameplay implementation and flexibility

• Implementing and maintaining online features such as matchmaking, invites and friends

• Profiling and improving network performance, bandwidth and latency, and making sure the game holds up on real-world connections

• Breaking down complex technical challenges, helping decide what to prioritise, and ensuring important decisions are understood by the people they affect

• Staying close to the actual game: writing production code, debugging difficult problems, and improving systems as the project evolves

**You’re a great match if

**

• You have at least ten years of professional game development experience across multiple shipped games and different stages of development, including significant technical ownership or leadership on a project

• You have experience setting technical direction and helping a programming team make and implement architectural decisions, with strong judgment in balancing flexibility, maintainability, performance and the needs of a creative production

• You're highly proficient in C# and have deep knowledge of the Unity engine and editor

• You've shipped at least one online multiplayer game, had real ownership of its networking/online systems, and have hands-on experience with a Unity multiplayer framework (e.g., Coherence)

• You communicate clearly and can explain technical decisions and trade-offs to programmers and non-programmers alike

**Nice to haves

**

• You have experience shipping iOS and macOS apps, including hands-on integration of Apple platform services such as GameKit and the Game Controller framework using Xcode and Swift

• Experience with backend services, dedicated servers or cloud hosting for online games

• Interest in multiplayer game design and social features

• Experience working with automated build pipelines such as Jenkins

• Experience building systemic or open-world games

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness and creativity while actively contributing to sustaining that culture

• You believe games are made by teams, not rockstars and that great ideas can come from anyone

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them

• You love exploration and experimentation but don’t get too precious when the evidence tells you you’re wrong

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place to be

**Practicalities

**

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• For this role we also consider people located outside of Denmark and provide financial (and moral!) support with visa application and relocation.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10-15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• Our working language is English.

**We offer

**

• Silly but ambitious projects, and the chance to work on and impact great games that reach millions of players.

• A playful and ambitious work environment where experimentation is encouraged.

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games.

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth.

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, team events, you name it.

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant just a walk across the lakes away, with plant-based options (and soft ice on Thursdays).

• Six weeks of vacation (five standard plus one extra on us).

• Paid parental leave at full salary for the periods covered by state reimbursement.

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked.

• Pension plan and private health insurance.

• Endless amounts of Faxe Kondi.

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, which is played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make everyone laugh. To do so, we focus on exploring comedy through gameplay. We like to break player expectations, use wonderful music, slick art, and create a quirky atmosphere. We experiment a lot, and it doesn't always work out, but we always learn something.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games, and we believe diversity makes for better teams. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and will challenge us and our way of doing things.

For more info about Triband, check out: triband.net/about

jobs.occupation: Manager – Bespoke Software Development & Adjacent Markets team
jobs.description:
Manager – Bespoke Software Development & Adjacent Markets team

Bring your software development expertise and leadership together in a role where people, technology and delivery meet. Lead a team across Aarhus and Warsaw, turn customer needs into customer-tailored Bespoke software solutions and connect Defence expertise with opportunities across Systematic. Along the way, help your team grow and shape AI adoption in developing software.

Your role: Drive software delivery and develop your team

As Manager in the SitaWare Extensions program, you will report to the Senior Director and lead one of the Defence Bespoke Development teams alongside the Adjacent Markets service function.

Your main focus will be delivering customer-tailored Bespoke software solutions that extends SitaWare Headquarters, Frontline and Edge – from software add-ons to system, tactical radio and military equipment integrations. You will take ownership of delivery on schedule, within budget and to the agreed quality. Alongside this, you will act as Project Manager for non-Defence business units in Systematic connecting them with Defence expertise, coordinating and delivering the services they need.

You can look forward to:

• Managing and driving software projects forward by setting priorities, aligning capacity and schedules, tracking progress and budgets, and managing stakeholders, risks and issues

• Developing your team across Aarhus and Warsaw through 1:1s, development talks, creating opportunities for professional and personal growth and recruitment

• Contributing your team's expertise to Defence bids for Bespoke software and representing Defence services in bids across other business units

• Building strong internal partnerships and coordinating communication on SitaWare releases, change requests, defect handling and hotfixes

• Shaping better ways of working, from processes and guides to the use of AI and agentic AI throughout the software development life cycle

You should expect 5–15 travel days a year.

Your team: Bringing SitaWare expertise together

You will lead 8–10 software architects, software engineers and test engineers across Aarhus and Warsaw, including interns and student workers, with a team lead already in place in Warsaw.

You will be part of a wider international network of colleagues across Defence Services, Product Development and other Systematic business units. The Adjacent Markets function draws on specialist expertise from other teams as needed, giving you a broad technical network and connections across the organisation.

You bring: Technical depth, people leadership and the drive to deliver

You combine a solid foundation in software development and architecture with experience guiding projects and leading people. Over several years as a project manager or software engineering manager, you have delivered medium to complex software projects or commercial off-the-shelf software products. You also bring some years of people management experience, an understanding of commercial customer contracts and experience providing services to other business units.

We are also looking for:

• A master’s degree in computer science, software engineering, software design and architecture, data science or cybersecurity, or equivalent

• Experience with system integration software, preferably within Defence, Maritime, Energy/Utilities, Transportation/Logistics or Healthcare, and with AI and agentic AI in the software development life cycle

• Confidence using Jira, D365 Project Management, Confluence and the Microsoft Office suite, including SharePoint, to support planning, collaboration and reporting

• Hands-on experience with technologies such as Java, C#, Angular, Docker, Git, deployment pipelines or cloud platforms is an advantage, along with any Defence domain knowledge from industry or the military

• Fluent English and the ability to bring clarity to technical discussions and collaboration across teams

• A proactive, decisive approach with strong ownership and follow-through, combined with the ability to motivate and involve people, put customers first, embrace change and communicate clearly with stakeholders at every level

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees Club, which offers nearly 100 events a year of both social and professional character. Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Start your development here

If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Thomas Frandsen Røjkjær, Director Extensions, Defence.

Communications Manager, Defence - Aarhus, Denmark

Do you want to shape how Systematic is seen across the Nordic defence sector, as the thought leader behind C5ISR software that supports allied forces every day? As our new Communications Manager, you will drive external communications for Systematic Defence in the Nordics working closely with international colleagues and taking real ownership of our story, from breaking news to speaker platforms.

The job

As Communications Manager, you will turn complex defence technology, customer developments and industry trends into clear, relevant stories for Nordic audiences. Working across Defence, Sales, Product Management and the international MarCom organisation, you will identify strong angles, engage subject-matter experts and take stories from idea to publication. You will also build trusted media relationships and help position Systematic and the SitaWare suite as an authoritative voice within C5ISR.

Some of your key tasks will be to:

• create content for media outlets and Systematic's own channels

• engage with internal and external sources and stakeholders to uncover and shape stories that position Systematic as a thought leader in C5ISR

• drive communication efforts around tradeshows and events, working closely with our international offices — particularly our Danish offices

• translate relevant international stories into Danish content

• support the wider positioning of Systematic and SitaWare across the Nordics

Expect around 30+ days of travel a year to Systematic offices, tradeshows and events.

Joining the team

You will join a collaborative Defence MarCom team of seven colleagues based across Aarhus, Cologne, Washington and Farnborough. Although we work across locations, we stay closely connected through daily collaboration on Teams and come together in person every six to eight weeks. You will also work closely with colleagues across Systematic Defence, bringing different perspectives and specialist expertise together to strengthen our position within C5ISR. Here, you will have the freedom to take ownership of your own stories and projects, while benefiting from the ideas, support and experience of an international, multi-skilled team.

What you bring

You bring at least eight years of relevant communications experience and a professional background in journalism, communications or marketing. You are an accomplished storyteller who can turn complex subject matter into clear, engaging content for different audiences and channels.

We are also looking for:

• experience working with Umbraco or another content management system

• familiarity with HubSpot or a similar marketing platform

• native-level Danish and fluency in written and spoken English

• independent, proactive and structured workstyle, combined with a collaborative mindset and the confidence to engage colleagues, subject-matter experts, journalists and other external stakeholders

• experience working in central government, the defence or technology sector would be an advantage

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years, as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

**Join Our Team

**We are looking for three Automation Engineers who are eager to develop their expertise and make an impact within a dynamic and supportive team. DESMI is a dynamic and innovative company where your ideas matter. We're building a culture that values collaboration, continuous learning, and making a difference. As an employee at DESMI, you'll have the opportunity to work on challenging projects, develop cutting-edge skills, and connect with a diverse team of talented individuals. If you're looking for a workplace where you can grow, contribute, and be inspired, DESMI is the place for you.

**Ideally, We Are Looking For Someone Who Is

**

• Curious and eager to explore new technologies and solutions

• Driven by solving technical challenges and delivering high-quality results

• Collaborative and motivated by working across disciplines to create robust solutions

**A glimpse into the role

**As an Automation Engineer, you will become part of a global Automation team with 8 colleagues in Denmark and 2 colleagues in China. Automation is a key strategic focus at DESMI, and you will play an important role in further developing and strengthening our automation solutions.

We are expanding our team and are looking for engineers with different strengths and interests. Whether your expertise lies in PLC and software development, electrical and hardware design, system integration, or technical leadership, you will help develop robust and reliable automation solutions across DESMI's product portfolio. Working closely with colleagues across Product Development, Engineering, Production, Service, and Sales, you will contribute to delivering high-quality solutions that create value for our customers.

**Depending on your strengths and interest, your main responsibilities could include:

**

• Development and maintenance of automation solutions for DESMI products and systems

• Design and implementation of PLC and HMI software

• Development and integration of electrical, control, and communication systems

• Participation in system testing, commissioning, and technical verification

• Preparation of technical documentation and support material

• Technical support for DESMI's global organization

• Driving continuous improvements of products, processes, and technical quality

• Ensuring solutions can be efficiently handed over to Production and Service

**Your next opportunity starts here

**As someone who will join our Automation Team, we are looking for a skilled engineer who is a self-driven individual with expertise in automation technology, electrical engineering, or a related field.

**We Also Imagine That You

**

• Have an educational background within Automation Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Software Engineering, or a related technical field

• Have experience with automation systems, PLC programming, electrical systems, or a combination of these disciplines

• Enjoy solving technical challenges and turning complex requirements into practical solutions

• Have a structured approach to your work and take ownership of your tasks

• Thrive in a collaborative environment and enjoy working with colleagues across functions and locations

• Communicate fluently in English, both written and spoken

It would be an advantage if you have experience with:

• PLC platforms such as Siemens Step 7 and TIA Portal

• Hardware design, electrical schematics, and documentation in SEE Electrical or similar CAD tools

• Industrial communication protocols such as OPC UA, MQTT, Modbus TCP/IP, or Profinet

• Pumping systems, water treatment systems, or other industrial applications

• Marine, defense, or other highly regulated industries

**The perks of being at DESMI

**At DESMI, we want you to feel supported, valued and motivated. That’s why we offer a range of benefits that make a difference – from flexibility and career opportunities to security.

Here are some of the benefits we offer our employees:

• Flexible working hours With the option to work from home two days a week, supporting a hybrid work environment that fosters productivity and teamwork.

• Global career prospects Be part of DESMI’s global team. Working with dedicated colleagues across Europe, Asia and USA.

• Skills development and career growth Opportunities for training, job rotation and internal mobility.

• Pension With employer contributions up to 10% depending on your contract type.

• Private healthcare and life insurance Your well-being is important to us. We provide comprehensive private healthcare coverage, giving you access to quality medical treatment when needed.

• On-site canteen Including a light breakfast, lunch buffet and fruit snacks throughout the day, with a focus on healthy and varied meals.

• Company sports & social activities Join events like badminton, bowling, summer parties, art clubs and more.

**What We’re About

**But we’re more than just pumps. At DESMI, we believe teamwork and innovation drive success.

**When You Join DESMI, You Can Expect

**

• A collaborative and supportive team environment.

• Opportunities for continuous learning and professional development.

• A chance to contribute your ideas and make a real impact.

• A company that values sustainability and innovation.

We are a flat organization with an open-door policy, where decisions are made together, and ideas are always welcome. Here, doers thrive – if you see an opportunity for improvement, you have the freedom to act on it.

As innovators in reliable and sustainable flow solutions, we serve a wide range of industries from Aquaculture and Defense to Green Technologies – the list goes on. Sustainability is highly appreciated while developing high-performance and long-lasting technologies that help industries adapt to evolving markets while reducing environmental impact.

**Ready to apply?

**If you're a motivated individual seeking a challenging and rewarding career where you can contribute to a more sustainable future, we encourage you to apply through the platform!

To learn more about this opportunity please contact Søren Flummer at sorf@desmi.com . We are reviewing applications on a rolling basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

As a Senior Service Engineer at DESMI, your primary responsibility is to install, service, maintain, and repair our customers’ products and equipment, primarily related to pumps. You will be responsible for ensuring that the products are serviced correctly, operate reliably, and meet the customers’ needs. Your role also involves delivering excellent customer service and maintaining strong relationships with our customers.

**Work Tasks

**Your work will include gaining knowledge of, or developing expertise in, our own pump range – particularly our centrifugal pumps used by district heating and industrial customers. You will also work with sprinkler units and pressure boosting systems at various customer sites. Work on equipment from other manufacturers should also be expected.

You will perform regular maintenance to ensure optimal performance of the equipment, identify and resolve faults during maintenance, and carry out repairs either on-site or at the company’s facilities. Troubleshooting and diagnosing faults, followed by implementing appropriate solutions, will often take place in close collaboration with the Service Manager.

Customer service is an important part of the role. You will deliver excellent customer service, respond to customer inquiries, and provide technical support and guidance when needed.

Documentation is also a key responsibility. You will be expected to complete accurate documentation of all tasks performed, including installations, maintenance, and repairs, and report back to management regarding status updates and any challenges encountered.

DESMI currently uses an IT-based Field Service system, so good IT skills and language skills are considered an advantage.

**About You

**

• We imagine that you have experience with installation, maintenance, and repair of technical products.

• Technical knowledge and skills relevant to our product range.

• You possess strong problem-solving abilities, good communication skills, and a customer-focused mindset.

• You are able to work independently and efficiently.

• Your background may include experience as an electrician, automotive mechanic, agricultural mechanic, electro-mechanic, marine engineer, or another relevant technical education or professional experience within the field.

DESMI offers a wide range of training courses depending on your current competencies.

It is necessary that you have a flexible approach to working hours and are prepared to perform service and repairs while systems are still in operation when required. We always strive to provide the best possible service to our customers, as fully functioning installations are essential to their operations. Much of our equipment forms part of critical infrastructure.

DESMI Denmark A/S’ service organization performs preventive maintenance, emergency troubleshooting, and repairs on all pump installations. Services are provided both on request and through established service agreements. As our new Service Technician, you will therefore work with many different types of pump applications. Currently, we primarily work with three product groups: submersible pump installations, dry-installed gear and centrifugal pumps, and sprinkler systems.

The department in Hvidovre currently consists of 12 service technicians and 4 office staff. In addition to the service department in Hvidovre, DESMI Denmark A/S also has service departments in Kolding and Nørresundby. Altogether, the service organization consists of 35 employees.

Have we caught your interest? We offer an exciting position with varied tasks and supportive colleagues in a working environment characterized by an informal tone and strong team spirit. If you have any questions about the position, you are welcome to contact Carsten Andersen at caan @desmi.com Please apply by clicking the “Apply” button below.

Facade Insulation Workers – Vejle, Denmark

jobs.description:
Clinical Associate Professor (Research) of Paediatrics (Fixed-term, 5 years)

  Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
 University of Copenhagen

   

  The University seeks to appoint a clinical associate professor (research) of Paediatrics to the Department of Clinical Medicine to commence as soon as possible.

  The clinical research professorship (research) is combined with a clinical position at Zealand University Hospital, Department of Paediatric and Adolescent Medicine.

  It is a requirement for appointment that the applicant is accepted for both the clinical associate professorship (research) and the clinical position. In order to be considered the applicant must send an application to both the Faculty (the clinical associate professorship (research)) and to the hospital (the clinical position) cf. the simultaneously advertised clinical position. This also applies to applicants who are already employed at the Hospital. Applicants should only apply for a clinical position at one of the hospitals. The advertisement for the clinical position is available from 

  Sundhedsjobs.dk - Clinical position as staff specialist combined with a clinical associate professorship (research) in Paediatrics- Børn og Unge, Sjællands Universitetshospital

  Information on the Department of Clinical Medicine, University of Copenhagen can be found at: Institut for Klinisk Medicin – Københavns Universitet

  Job description

  The clinical associate professors’ (research) duties will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research - Conduct and lead research on the development, treatment, and outcomes of diabetes in children and adolescents. The research is anchored in the Clinical Research Unit, Department of Paediatric and Adolescent Medicine, and carried out in collaboration with departments at Zealand University Hospital, other hospitals, and regional and national research partners. Responsibilities include dissemination of research findings through peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and other academic activities. 	
• Research-based teaching – Deliver pregraduate teaching and examinations as part of the Clinical Course in Paediatrics for medical students, including lectures and student-centred learning activities such as tutorials. Supervise bachelor’s, master’s, and PhD students, and contribute to teaching within the mandatory Research Training Programme for Doctors in Specialist Training. 	
• Research leadership - Co-leadership of the Clinical Research Unit in the Department of Paediatric and Adolescent Medicine. Conduct independent research and development activities, and provide academic leadership, mentorship, and supervision for early-career researchers. 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society – Contribute to the dissemination of scientific knowledge to healthcare professionals, patients, policymakers, and the wider public. 	
• Academic assessments – Participation in academic assessment and evaluation activities as a member of the assessor group within the Department of Clinical Medicine.   The division between the different tasks may vary over the 5-year period of employment. Teaching obligations are equivalent to a previous external clinical associate professorship rate B.

  Any current employment as clinical associate professor (rate A, B or rate C) will expire if the applicant is employed as a clinical associate professor (research).

  Required qualifications 

  The qualification requirement for the clinical associate professor (research) is a master’s degree in medicine, specialist status as well as further teaching and research qualifications, for example PhD or doctorate and subsequently documented scientific production on an international level. In addition, there will be an emphasis on experience with scientific guidance, research administration and international research collaboration.

  The clinical associate professors (research) are also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Terms of employment

  A clinical associate professor (research) is paid in accordance with Aftale om kliniske lektorer af 11. februar 2024 mellem Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet, Foreningen af Speciallæger og Yngre Læger, Cirkulære om aftale om kliniske lektorer ved universiteter under Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and Akademikerne (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations. The position is covered by the current Ministerial Order on the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.

  Questions

  For further information please contact Deputy Head of Department of Clinical Medicine, Professor Lone Baandrup, lone.baandrup@regionh.dk 

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen – University of Copenhagen

  Application

  The application must be submitted in English and must include the following:

   	
• Application (Including motivations for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• A complete list of publications 	
• List of 5 publications to be considered in the assessment (Please note that we do not you to upload a copy of the 5 publications) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD and other relevant certificates) 	
• Self-declaration form (https://ikm.ku.dk/ansat/ansaettelser/dokumenter/self-declaration-form-klf.docx) 	
• Teaching portfolio (https://ikm.ku.dk/ansat/ansaettelser/dokumenter/template-teaching-portfolio.docx (English) or https://ikm.ku.dk/ansat/ansaettelser/dokumenter/skabelon-undervisningsportfolio.doc (Danish)) 	
• Research plan (3‐5 pages) 	
• Teaching plan   Application procedure 

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The head of department  appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at jobportal.ku.dk.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

  Please submit the application with the required attachments. Only online applications will be accepted. The closing date for applications is 23.59pm, Monday 30 November 2026.

  Interviews for this position will most likely be held in the month of March 2027.
